title: The 10 Best Corded Snow Blowers
subtitle: Plug-in snow blowers and electric snow shovels for driveways, walks and decks, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: Corded snow removal comes in two sizes. Electric snow shovels (10-16 in wide) clear steps, decks and walks; walk-behind blowers (20-22 in) handle driveways. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Westinghouse, Snow Joe, WEN, PowerSmart, DEKOPRO, SENIX and Earthwise on rating, review volume and features (a path 20 in or wider, a steel auger, a 12 in or deeper intake, a throw of 25 ft or more and LED lights). None of them comes with the outdoor-rated extension cord you'll need.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

buyers_guide.a: A corded blower never runs out of battery and costs less: the 20-22 in blowers here run $140-$250, against $270 and up for a battery blower of similar width with its pack. The trade-off is the cord. You're limited to how far an extension cord reaches, and you have to keep it clear of the auger.

buyers_guide.q: What extension cord do I need?
buyers_guide.a: An outdoor-rated cord in the gauge and length your blower's manual specifies. Snow Joe says not to go over 100 ft. A cord that's too long or too thin starves a 15 A motor, so buy the heaviest gauge the manual allows.

An electric snow shovel (10-16 in) is a handheld auger you push like a shovel. The ones here weigh 12-16 lb and suit steps, decks and walks after a few inches. A walk-behind blower (20-22 in) rolls on wheels, takes 10-13 in of snow per pass and clears a driveway much faster.

A single-stage blower's auger scrapes the pavement. A steel or rubber-tipped steel auger stands up to packed snow and ice chunks better than plastic. Westinghouse and DEKOPRO list steel augers; several other listings don't say, and Snow Joe's SJ627E listing says both.

buyers_guide.q: How deep a snowfall can a corded blower handle?
buyers_guide.a: The listed intake depth is the limit for one pass: 6-8 in for the snow shovels, 10-13 in for the blowers here (PowerSmart lists 6 in). For deeper or wet, heavy snow, take it in two passes or clear it before it piles up. The plowed-in pile at the end of the driveway is two-stage gas territory.
